correctness.rationale: For side sizes >=3, the common-neighbor formula S(x,y) identifies the bipartition, the intrinsic nonedge D(x,y) identifies exactly the removed matching and P identifies matched endpoints. Scoping the S,P subformulas reuses at most max(3,j) names while counting j matched or unmatched vertices on a side. These formulas separate every unequal clipped invariant; an indefinite k-pebble strategy preserving side, unmatched-vertex and matched-pair indices handles equal invariants. The four parameter regimes give precisely (k^3+4k^2-7k-2)/2 theories for k>=3. Complete finite model checks agree for 50 small instances at width three and independent structural tests cover 168 models. Finite checks are explicitly not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The family G(a,b,t) with a,b>=3 and matching deletion is a natural and substantially studied three-parameter graph family. The classification reconstructs an unnamed bipartition and missing matching in three variables, identifies the two independent unmatched-side size thresholds, yields the exact cubic theory spectrum and smallest representatives, and gives sharp width hierarchy examples. This materially extends the one-parameter balanced crown case rather than merely renaming or recomputing it.
